messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: model-fit evals / tool-calling & structured-output (next steps)

Hi Alex -

Thanks again for the call today - really helpful to get context on FinTechCo's reconciliation workflow and the constraints around latency (95th pctl < 250ms for single-turn lookups) and schema accuracy for downstream accounting systems. Quick summary / next steps from my side: 

- Use case: realtime transaction enrichment + categorical mapping -> requires JSON schema conformity for every API response (invalid responses must be <0.1% in production).
- Success metrics: schema-match rate, precision on merchant-category labels, and per-request median latency.
- Data ask: can you share a small set of masked sample records (PII removed) so we can run a quick fit/eval?
- Technical next step: we'll propose 2 model+inference configs to test (1 low-latency quantized variant, 1 higher-quality FP16 variant) and run structured-output evals (schema compliance + retry/idempotency checks).

Attached: redwood_benchmarks_q1_2026.pdf (high-level perf/quality of suggested models) and a starter prompt set (prompt_sets.zip).

Proposed timeline:
- This week: you share masked samples + definition of required output JSON schema
- Next week: we run internal evals and share results + recommended config
- Week after: tech deep-dive (30-45m) to run a sample through the pipeline with your engineers

Can you confirm you can send the masked samples and the schema by EOD Wednesday your time? Also flag any procurement or security reviewers we should loop in.

Thanks -
Marissa
Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: redwood_benchmarks_q1_2026.pdf, prompt_sets.zip

Marissa -

Thanks for the recap and the materials. Quick answers:

- We'll target the 95th pctl latency you listed; any suggestions on token/request shaping that will help meet it are welcome.
- Attached is a small masked sample set: FinTechCo_PII_masked_samples.csv (100 rows). Data team removed PII but left tricky edge cases for categories.
- Our required output schema is attached as a JSON Schema in the file "fintechco_output_schema.json" (see link below).

Primary concerns: we've seen regressions when model updates changed how functions/tool-calling returned nested arrays - we need strict guarantees around schema stability and a clear retry strategy for transient model errors.

Links:
- Schema (internal link): https://fintechco.box.com/s/fintechco_output_schema.json

CCing our engineering lead is optional - she prefers to join the tech deep-dive if we get to that stage.

Best,

alex.j@fintechco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model-fit evals / tool-calling & structured-output (recommendations + eval plan)

Alex - thanks for the sample and schema link. High-level recommendations below; we'll follow up with a short report after running the sample through our eval harness.

1) Model recommendations (initial test matrix):
- "redwood-llama2-13b-q4f16" (quantized) - lowest latency, good baseline for schema adherence when combined with strict function-calling enforcement.
- "redwood-instruct-30b-fp16" - higher-quality outputs, recommended if you prioritize label accuracy over per-request tail latency.

2) Benchmarks & artifacts:
- Raw perf/quality matrix: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-redwood-fintech-benchmarks
- Starter prompt sets: attached (prompt_sets.zip). We'll expand prompts to hit edge cases in your samples.

3) Structured-output eval approach:
- Schema compliance: we validate model outputs against your JSON Schema on every request; we surface the exact validation error for failed responses and compute a schema-match rate. Target: >99.9% in eval before moving to canary.
- Function/tool-calling: we run both explicit function-calls (where the model returns structured args) and optional post-processing layers to enforce types. We capture mismatch patterns (missing keys, wrong types, unexpected nulls).
- Retries & idempotency: Redwood supports configurable retry policies at the routing layer - standard plan is up to 2 automatic retries with exponential backoff + deterministic idempotency keys so downstream systems see one effective action. We'll include tests for duplicated-suppression and ordering.

4) Quality regressions:
- We'll run a regression test suite against your canonical prompt set; if we detect a drop in label precision >2% compared to the baseline model, we'll flag for manual review and rollback options.

Next steps I'll do this week: run the masked samples through both recommended configs, produce a short results deck (schema-match rate, per-label precision, latency distribution), and propose a 30m tech deep-dive for next Thursday.

If that sounds good, I'll schedule the deep-dive and send an invite to the FinTechCo engineers.

Thanks -
Marissa

Attachments: (none)
Related links: https://docs.redwood.com/evals/structured-output-guidelines

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Tech asks for structured-output evals (FinTechCo)

Rishi / Aditya -

Looping you in on FinTechCo (DEAL-2026-1023). They sent masked samples and a JSON Schema. Can you cover the following: 

- Run both configs I recommended: redwood-llama2-13b-q4f16 and redwood-instruct-30b-fp16 on the sample set. Produce: schema-match rate, per-label precision/recall, latency p50/p95.
- For function-calling: test both explicit function-call API mode and a post-processor enforcement layer. Report failure modes (missing keys, type mismatches) and example counterexamples.
- Retry testing: simulate transient model errors and measure idempotency key behavior; confirm retries don't produce duplicate downstream actions for identical requests.
- Deliverable: short deck + runbook with recommended routing policy (retry counts, backoff, model pinned for canary).

I'll share the results with Alex and propose the tech deep-dive. Aim to have a first-pass by EOD Friday.

Thanks -
Marissa

(Do not include FinTechCo raw samples outside the secure eval cluster.)
